battle.name: 吉備氏之亂
battle.theater: 備前國吉備郡（岡山市東南）
battle.brief: 463年，備前國吉備氏頭領弟熊舉兵反亂，與倭王朝廷在吉備郡一帶對抗，經追討而平，首謀者被斬並梟首送京。卡面羅馬短劍並未隨軍東渡，但大和陣中的鐵短刀與其同屬短兵刺擊的技術路數，在近身衝突裡扮演了歐陸盾後短劍的角色。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 吉備氏之亂發生於463年，即敏達天皇時期的永寧三年，是倭王朝廷與大和地方部族首長之間的一場正面衝突。朝廷一方以大和的王庭為核心：敏達天皇當時尚未即位，以皇子的身分主持軍事，實際統兵的是大伴氏等伴造一系的軍事部族，命令由中臣氏等神職部族以告文與祭祀的方式傳達，兵員則由秦氏、漢氏等渡來系部族以及諸郡豪族所部的部眾湊成。這是一個尚未經過律令制度整編的編織：王的名義、氏族的實力、部民的應徵，構成三層權力結構，朝廷能下命令，卻沒有集中的營與統一的後勤。叛亂一方是備前國吉備郡的吉備氏，即史籍所稱的吉備臣或吉備造，首領為弟熊；其部眾來自吉備郡及周邊諸郡的部族，並可能得到播磨方向地方勢力的呼應，行動目標是脫離朝廷的徵發與祭祀分擔，恢復部首長的自主權。雙方實力無法量化：朝廷握有王的名分與調動數部的餘地，吉備氏則握有地形熟悉、氏族團結與部民忠誠的優勢。戰事集中在備前至播磨的山間通道一帶，這是一場內戰性質的地方首長叛乱，而不是兩國之間的戰爭。
countriesEn: The Kibi rising broke out in 463 CE, the third year of the Eei reign in the time of the future Emperor Bidatsu, and it was a head-on clash between the Yamato court and a local clan head in the provinces. The court side was centred on the Yamato royal house. Prince Hotatsu had not yet taken the throne and directed the campaign in the person of a prince, but the troops were actually led by the Otomo and the other military clans of the tomo-tsukuri line; the orders of the court were conveyed by the Nakatomi and the other priestly clans through proclamation and ritual; and the levies were made up of the immigrant clans such as the Hata and the Han, together with the war bands of the great houses of the several districts. This was an organisation not yet regularised by the ritsuryo system: the authority of the king, the real power of the great families and the service of the be formed three separate layers of power. The court could issue orders, but it had no centralised corps and no unified logistics. The rebel side was the Kibi clan of Kibi district in Bizen province, the Kibi no Omi or Kibi no Muraji of the records, headed by Otomaro. Their followers were drawn from the clans of Kibi district and of the neighbouring districts, and may have been answered by local interests further towards Harima; their object was to escape the levies of the court and its share of ritual obligations, and to recover the autonomy of the clan head. The balance of strength cannot be quantified: the court held the legitimacy of the king and the margin for calling out several be, while the Kibi held familiarity with the ground, cohesion of the clan and the loyalty of the be. The fighting was concentrated along the mountain tracks between Bizen and Harima, and this was in nature a civil war fought by local forces rather than a war between two states.
people: 關鍵人物方面，叛軍一方的核心是弟熊，史籍記作吉備臣弟熊或吉備造弟熊，是吉備氏的部首。他以自己的名義起兵，率部眾在吉備郡及周邊與朝廷的討伐軍對抗，兵敗之後被追捕、遭斬，首級送達京城。朝廷方面的最高統帥是敏達天皇，他此時尚未即位，以皇子的身分主持討伐，戰後於479年即位，486年去世；與他同時在事的是當時的皇太子大郎子，也就是後來的雄略天皇。兄弟二人在王位繼承與部族任用上一直存在緊張，記錄裡兩人都與戰事相關，但誰先抵陣、誰掌握實際指揮，歷來說法不一，學界多把這點視為這場內亂背後真正的緊張所在。軍務由大伴氏一系承擔，伴造在大和握有調度部眾、率領集團的實權，是王庭的武力支柱；同樣長期活動於備前一帶的渡來系秦氏以鍛鐵見名，日後秦氏的抬頭常被上推到這段時期，說明此役牽動的不只是吉備一家。隨侍的武職有稚子這類尚武之人，派遣正使的慣例則同時存在。5世紀大和正維持密集的對外往來，462年向高麗、百濟、新羅、任那等國遣使，476年又有倭王武遣使劉宋的記載，這些背景與內亂同期。整體而言，這場戰爭的人事記錄非常簡略，除弟熊與敏達、大郎子之外，具名者極少，連首謀者身邊的部族首長也沒有留下名字，這正是它長期被研究卻始終不夠確定的原因。
peopleEn: As for the key figures, the core of the rebel side was Otomaro, recorded as Kibi no Omi Otomaro or Kibi no Muraji Otomaro, who was the head of the Kibi clan. He raised the rising in his own name and led his followers against the punitive force of the court in Kibi district and its neighbourhood; after the defeat he was hunted down and beheaded, and his head was brought to the capital. The supreme commander on the court side was Prince Hotatsu, the future Emperor Bidatsu, who had not yet taken the throne and directed the campaign in the person of a prince, was crowned in 479 and died in 486. Alongside him in the affair was the crown prince of the time, Otarō, who was later to become Emperor Yōryaku. The two brothers were under lasting tension over the succession and over the use of the great clans; the record has both of them connected with the war, but who reached the field first and who held the real command has been read in many ways, and most scholars take this to be the real tension behind the rising. The military work was carried by the line of the Otomo: the tomo-tsukuri held the real power of calling out be and leading groups in Yamato, and were the armed pillar of the royal house. The immigrant Hata, who were also active for long in the Bizen area, were famous for their iron working, and the later rise of the Hata is often traced back to this period, which shows that the affair drew in more than the single house of Kibi. Among those attending the princes were martial men of the wakaji kind, and the practice of sending formal envoys existed at the same time. Fifth-century Yamato was sustaining dense foreign contacts: envoys were sent to Goguryeo, Paekche, Silla and Jina in 462, and in 476 there is the record of the king of Wa, Wudi, sending an embassy to the Liu Song. The record of persons for this war is in any case very thin: apart from Otomaro and the two princes, very few are named, and not even the clan leaders around the chief rebel have left their names behind, which is precisely why the rising has been studied for so long yet never quite settled.
kits: 卡面這把羅馬短劍並沒有出現在463年的大和陣中。它是羅馬共和末期到帝國前期軍團步兵的制式短刺劍，刃長約半米出頭，單刃，刃形呈菱形或葉形，握柄裝有圓盤狀的護手，用途只有一個：在護盾之後、或盾與盾之間的窄縫裡，以短促的刺擊解決迎面的人。它不是用來揮砍的，斬殺與劈砍另有長劍與斧劍負責；短劍與一人多高的曲面大盾、鎖子甲及頭盔構成一套完整的裝備體系。大和陣中功能相近的，是同樣用來做短刺動作的鐵製短兵：短刀、環頭大刀一類的短刺用刀，以及更早傳入的曲刃猪牙劍；這類短刃體量輕、不追求斬切，重心放在突進時的一刺，配合的是弓矢而不是長矛的正面對撞。5世紀的大和作戰，遠射主力是弓：和弓的弓身長約一米上下，矢長六七十厘米，鏃用鐵或石；近戰則是槍（長柄上裝半月形鐵刃）與短刀並用；防護只有木、革、竹製的楯，鎧甲十分稀少，沒有任何接近歐陸重裝步兵全身甲胄的東西。馬匹已廣泛使用，但主要作騎乘與傳令，獨立的騎兵兵種尚未成形。攻城沒有投石機與衝車，靠的是部族的城邑、柵垣與壕溝；制度化的築城防禦要晚到推古朝586年的詔令才出現，以屯倉為名的據點更在7世紀中葉。糧秣靠田租與部族的徵發，運補依山陰道與河川的水路。總之，羅馬短劍代表的是盾後短刺那一整套歐陸軍制下的近戰邏輯；它在吉備氏之亂裡的位置是一面鏡子，照見同一時代的列島上，一支以弓矢與短刀為主、幾乎沒有甲胄的隊伍，如何在密林與丘陵之間打另一種戰爭。
kitsEn: The Roman gladius on the card did not appear in the Yamato army of 463. It was the standard short stabbing sword of the Roman legionary infantry from the late Republic into the early Empire: the blade was a little over half a metre, single edged, lozenge- or leaf-shaped, with a disc-shaped pommel at the hilt, and it had exactly one purpose, to settle the man in front of you with a short thrust from behind the shield or from the gap between two shields. It was not made to swing; cutting and chopping were the work of longer swords and of the axe. The gladius formed part of a complete equipment system with a tall curved shield, a mail shirt and a helmet. The nearest functional counterparts in the Yamato ranks were the iron short weapons used for the same short stabbing action: short swords, the short stabbing blades of the ring-pommel type such as the kentō tachi, and the curved-bladed magatana swords that had entered the islands much earlier. Such short blades were light, made no pretence at cutting, and put their weight on a single thrust delivered while advancing, and they worked together with the bow rather than with the head-on clash of long spears. In fifth-century Yamato warfare the main ranged arm was the bow: the yumi had a bow of about a metre, arrows of sixty to seventy centimetres, with points of iron or of stone. Close combat combined the spear, with a half-moon iron blade on a long haft, with the short sword. Protection amounted to shields of wood, leather or bamboo; armour was very rare, and nothing at all came near the full harness of the heavy infantry of the Mediterranean. Horses were already widely used, but chiefly for riding and for carrying messages, and a separate mounted arm had not yet taken shape. Siege work had no stone-thrower and no battering ram, and depended on the fortified settlements of the clans, on fences and on ditches; a systematic policy of building fortified positions appears only with the edict of 586 under Prince Shotoku, and the stockade forts called tunkō come later still, in the mid seventh century. Grain came from the land tax and from the levy of the clans, and supply moved along the Yamashiro road and by water. In sum, the gladius stands for the logic of close combat in the European system of fighting from behind a shield; in the Kibi rising its function is that of a mirror, showing how a force armed mainly with bow and short sword, and with almost no armour, fought a different kind of war in the forests and hills of the same age.
tactics: 作戰方式上，朝廷方依循大和既有的傳統：以王的名義發布告令，命大伴氏等軍事部族率部眾討伐，同時命中部地區的豪族承擔方任，把討伐任務分解給各郡的部首長；這是一種以部族為單位的徵發，沒有集中的營編制，也沒有統一後勤，糧秣與道路全靠各部自備。追擊的方向大致沿備前向播磨一線的山間通道展開，叛軍據城邑、扼谷口，以弓矢射擊追兵，再在狹窄處以短兵反擊；短兵在其中的作用，正像歐陸方陣裡短劍在盾牆縫隙中的位置，只是這裡沒有盾牆，只有密林、梯田與竹叢。防禦方善用地形切割追兵，縱火焚燒糧秣與村舍，截斷道路，切斷部眾之間的聯繫，迫使遠征的朝廷軍缺糧而退。朝廷方則以人海與分割持久戰耗對手：先以一部兵力圍逼據點、斷其外援，再以另一部搜索游擊集團，首要目標不是斬首，而是斬斷部族的團結，把首謀者從部眾中孤立出來。戰後的處置同樣是部族式的：編戶還籍，重新指定部首長，把俘獲與財貨分賜有功諸部，把吉備氏的勢力拆散為若干更小的部。關於戰役的具體過程、日期與經過地點，傳世記錄極為簡略，幾乎每一處細節都有不同解讀；較為可靠的是結果與方向，而不是戰術序列。
tacticsEn: In method, the court followed the established practice of Yamato: it issued proclamations in the name of the king, ordered the military clans such as the Otomo to lead their be against the rebels, and at the same time assigned the great houses of the several districts a share in the campaign, breaking the task of suppression up among the clan heads of each district. This was a levy organised by clan: there was no centralised corps, no unified logistics, and grain and roads were the responsibility of each be itself. The direction of pursuit ran along the mountain tracks from Bizen towards Harima. The rebels held their settlements and their valley mouths, shot at the pursuing columns with their bows, and answered at close quarters with short weapons in the narrow places. The short weapon played there the part that the gladius played in the gaps of a European shield wall, except that here there was no shield wall at all, only forest, terraced fields and bamboo. The defenders used the ground to cut the pursuers up, burned grain and farmsteads, blocked the roads and severed the links between the be, so that the court's far-ranging columns ran short of food and had to fall back. The court in turn wore the opponent down with numbers and with a war of separate columns: first one body invested the strongpoints and cut them off from outside help, then another searched out the roaming bands; the first object was not to take the chief's head but to break the cohesion of the clan and isolate the leader from his own people. The settlement after the war was likewise of a clan kind: the be were enrolled again, the clan heads were reappointed, prisoners and booty were distributed among the meritorious, and the power of the Kibi was broken up into a number of smaller be. The transmitted record of the actual course of the war, of its dates and of the places it passed through is extremely thin, and almost every detail has more than one reading. The result and the direction of the campaign are the reliable part; the sequence of tactics is not.
data: 能夠核對的數字不多，而且多數與戰役本身無關。第一類是年表：起事繫於463年，即敏達天皇時期的永寧三年，許多研究以462年春夏間的舉兵、463年朝廷大軍壓境，到464年平定，中間跨越一個完整年度；由於《日本書紀》卷二十四「敏達天皇即位前紀」是這段事蹟唯一的詳盡來源，它的年次編排與後世年表存在若干出入，具體月份至今沒有定論，一般繫於五月前後。兵力、傷亡與戰利品的數字完全沒有留下來：這部史書記戰役多用發兵、討平一類的敘述，記的是事件與命令，不是戰術報告。第二類是編制數字：5世紀大和的兵制單位是部，每一部由一名部首長率領，部眾是世襲的勞役與兵役人口；朝廷一次能調動多少部，史料沒有給出答案。第三類是同期可交叉參照的外交數字：462年倭王向高麗、百濟、新羅、任那等國派遣使節，476年宋書記載倭國王武遣使劉宋；這兩件事說明大和在吉備氏之亂前後正處於對外接觸的高峰，內亂是與此並行的。第四類是考古數字：岡山縣備前一帶的5世紀古墳出土過鐵鏃、鐵刀、環頭大刀與馬具，可見當地的配備與鍛鐵傳統，這些器物能說明裝備，卻不能說明這場戰爭的規模。第五類是無法核實的推估：叛軍的作戰人數大概在數千的量級，主要靠吉備郡及周邊的部民，武力核心是吉備氏的常備眾；朝廷一方能集結的部眾可能更多，但戰鬥力的換算完全不可靠。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and most of them have nothing to do with the battle itself. The first class is the chronology. The rising is dated to 463 CE, the third year of the Eei reign in the time of the future Emperor Bidatsu; many studies set the outbreak in the spring or summer of 462, the arrival of the court's great army in 463, and the settlement by 464, so that a full year is covered. Since the passage of the Nihon Shoki, volume 24, in the preface to the reign of Emperor Bidatsu, is the only detailed source for this affair, its year numbering does not quite agree with later chronologies, and the exact month is still unsettled, being generally tied to around the fifth month. Figures for strength, for casualties and for booty are simply not preserved: the chronicle narrates the war with such formulas as raising troops and suppressing the enemy, recording events and orders rather than a tactical report. The second class is the numbers of organisation: the unit of the military in fifth-century Yamato was the be, each led by a clan head, its members being hereditary labour and service; how many be the court could call out at once, the sources do not say. The third class is the diplomatic figures from the same years that can be used as a cross-check: in 462 the king of Wa sent envoys to Goguryeo, Paekche, Silla and Jina, and in 476 the Song shu records the king of Wa, Wudi, sending an embassy to the Liu Song. These two facts show that Yamato was at the height of its foreign contacts around the Kibi rising, and that the civil war ran alongside them. The fourth class is archaeological: fifth-century tomb mounds in the Bizen area of Okayama Prefecture have yielded iron points, iron knives, ring-pommel swords and horse gear, so that the local equipment and the traditions of iron working are visible; such objects speak about equipment, not about the scale of this war. The fifth class is estimate, and cannot be verified: the rebel field strength was probably in the order of thousands, drawn mainly from the be of Kibi district and its neighbourhood, with the Kibi's own standing war band as the hard core; the court could muster more be, but any conversion of that into fighting strength is wholly unreliable.
cause: 打起來的原因，是中央王權在5世紀上半葉要處理的一個結構性問題。大和的倭王從4世紀末起已能向朝鮮半島與江南派遣使節，並在列島內部組織跨郡的軍事行動，徵發的規模與頻率都在上升；每一次遠征都要從備前、備中、播磨這些靠近山陰道與大道的大郡抽人、抽糧、抽馬，而每一次徵發，都意味著地方部首長把部民交出去之後，還要自己承擔隊伍的補給與損失。吉備氏是備前國最有力的部族之一，與渡來系秦氏的鐵工技術往來密切，在自己的地盤上握有鍛冶、鐵器與馬匹的資源；當朝廷的徵發越來越頻密，這種自主的部族經濟與受徵發的部族身份之間的矛盾便會積累。第二個原因是王位繼承的裂痕：敏達天皇與皇太子大郎子之間的角力，使追討吉備氏的指揮權本身成為皇族內部爭執的一部分，記錄裡兩位皇子都與戰事相關，這很可能就是亂事久久不能迅速平息的制度性原因。第三個原因是祭祀與神權的爭端：叛軍的首領以自己的氏族名義起兵，與朝廷中臣氏獨佔的祭祀權直接衝突；在以神意決定征與治的時代，宣布某氏族不服本身就是政治宣言。第四個原因是地理：備前位於山陰道與中國山地丘陵之間，森林密布、河流縱橫，道路狹窄而不利於大軍展開，地方武裝在此地的優勢遠高於平原，任何一次中央討伐都要付出額外的時間代價。第五個原因是外部牽制：大和當時正全力經營半島外交，任何內亂都可能被周邊政權利用，這也說明朝廷必須迅速平亂。
causeEn: The reason for the war was a structural problem that the central royal power had to deal with in the first half of the fifth century. From the late fourth century the king of Wa had been able to send envoys to the Korean peninsula and to the Jiangnan region, and had been organising military action across the several districts of the islands; the scale and the frequency of the levies were both rising. Every distant expedition drew men, grain and horses from the great districts lying along the Yamashiro road and the main highways, such as Bizen, Bitchu and Harima, and every levy meant that a local clan head, having handed over his people, still had to bear the supply and the losses of the column on top of it. The Kibi were among the strongest clans of Bizen province, were in close contact with the iron working of the immigrant Hata, and held the resources of forging, of iron and of horses within their own territory; as the levies of the court grew more frequent, the contradiction between an autonomous clan economy and a clan status as a source of levies would accumulate. The second cause was the fissure in the succession. The rivalry between Prince Hotatsu and the crown prince Otarō made the command of the pursuit itself part of a struggle inside the royal house, and the record connects both princes with the war; this is very probably the institutional reason why the affair was not settled quickly. The third cause was a conflict over ritual and priestly authority. The rebel leader raised the rising in the name of his own clan, which came into direct collision with the monopoly of the Nakatomi over sacrifice; in an age when the decision to make war and to govern was held to come from the gods, to declare that a clan would not obey was itself a political proclamation. The fourth cause was geography. Bizen lies between the Yamashiro road and the mountains and hills of the Chinese interior, with dense forest and rivers running in every direction; the roads are narrow and unfavourable to the deployment of a large army, and local armed strength is far stronger here than on open ground, so that every central punitive expedition costs extra time. The fifth cause was the pull from outside. Yamato was then working hard on its peninsula diplomacy, and any civil disorder might be taken advantage of by the neighbouring powers, which is also why the court had to end the rising quickly.
impact: 吉備氏之亂的規模不大，但它在5世紀中葉的大和留下幾道痕跡。第一，部族自治的邊界被重新劃定：平亂之後朝廷沒有把吉備郡的部眾編入律令式的行政，而是拆散原有的氏族紐帶，改以中原的豪族擔任方任，並把部分土地與部眾分賜有功的伴造與渡來系部族；備前一帶的權力結構因此改組，5世紀下半葉至6世紀活躍於備前及讃岐一帶的秦氏，其抬頭常被學者上推至此役之後。第二，皇族的用人格局改變：大郎子即位為雄略天皇之後，朝廷的對策逐漸由皇族領兵轉向依靠大伴氏等軍事部族，這條路線最終通向6世紀上半葉蘇我氏與大伴氏輪流掌權的局面，也種下了7世紀壬申之亂的遠因。第三，史料層面的影響尤其持久：這段記事之所以能留到今天，靠的是《日本書紀》敏達天皇即位前紀所收的簡短記錄，以及7世紀上半葉律令國家在壬申年造史時對《日本書紀》的整理；一部原本帶有強烈政治立場的王朝史，就這樣為5世紀中葉留下了孤本式的記載，使得這場內亂的年表、人物與結局都還能被討論。第四，這場內亂與大和對朝鮮半島的外交重疊在一起：平亂之後，462年派遣五韓使節、476年倭王武遣使劉宋這類動作得以持續進行，說明中央對地方的控制在平亂之後反而更為有效；5世紀末倭王向劉宋朝貢、並被《宋書》記為倭國王武的事件，也就建立在這樣的國內整合之上。
impactEn: The Kibi rising was small in scale, but it left several marks on Yamato in the middle of the fifth century. First, the boundaries of clan autonomy were redrawn. After the rising was put down, the court did not enrol the be of Kibi district into a ritsuryo administration; it broke up the old ties of kinship, made great houses from the central provinces take on the duty of fukura as local sponsors, and granted lands and be to the meritorious tomo-tsukuri and to the immigrant clans. The structure of power in the Bizen area was thereby reorganised, and the rise of the Hata in Bizen and Sanuki from the second half of the fifth to the sixth century is often pushed back by scholars to the aftermath of this war. Second, the pattern of employing men at court changed: after Otarō came to the throne as Emperor Yōryaku, the court's answer shifted gradually from princes leading the army in person to reliance on military clans such as the Otomo; that line of policy led in the end to the alternation of power between the Soga and the Otomo in the first half of the sixth century, and planted the remote seed of the Ninshin disturbance of the seventh century. Third, the effect on the historical record is the most durable of all. This episode survives only because of the brief notice preserved in the preface to the reign of Emperor Bidatsu in the Nihon Shoki, and because of the reorganisation of that chronicle when the ritsuryo state compiled its history in the ninshin year of the seventh century. A dynastic history written with strong political colouring has thus left a copy of a sort for the middle of the fifth century, so that the chronology, the persons and the outcome of the rising can still be discussed. Fourth, the rising overlapped with Yamato's diplomacy towards the Korean peninsula. After the rising was settled, actions such as the dispatch of envoys to the five Korean states in 462 and the embassy of the king of Wa, Wudi, to the Liu Song in 476 could go on, which shows that the centre's control over the localities became more effective rather than less once the rising was over; the appearance of the king of Wa before the Liu Song at the end of the fifth century, recorded in the Song shu as the king of Wa, rests on such a domestic settlement.
result: 起兵最終沒有成功。朝廷的討伐軍在吉備郡一帶逐步壓制了叛軍的據點，弟熊在戰敗之後被追捕並被斬，首級送到京師；追隨他的部眾失去首領與根據地，一部分被殺或被俘，一部分散回各自的部落，重編成朝廷可以控制的小部。吉備氏作為一個獨立的政治與軍事力量就此衰落下來，其首領權不再集中，備前一帶的部眾重新編入朝廷的徵發體系，朝廷也藉此把備前、備中、播磨一線的守備與稅賦納入更直接的監督。此後數十年，5世紀後半的大和沒有再出現同等規模的地方首長叛乱，與朝鮮半島的往來反而更為頻繁。可以確定的是：這場戰爭以朝廷的完全勝利告終，首謀者伏誅，勢力被拆散，秩序被重建。不能確定的是它的具體經過——陣亡人數、兵員、日期、乃至參戰部隊的具體構成，在傳世文獻裡幾乎全部空白；唯一可以確定的是，首謀者伏誅與首級送京的記載，以及朝廷得以重新掌握備前一線的結果。這正是它至今仍是一場知道結果而不知過程的戰爭的原因。
resultEn: The rising did not succeed in the end. The punitive force of the court gradually crushed the strongpoints of the rebels in the Kibi area, and after his defeat Otomaro was hunted down and beheaded, his head being carried to the capital. The followers who had stood with him lost both their leader and their base: some were killed or taken prisoner, and some scattered back to their own villages and were reorganised into the small be that the court could control. The Kibi clan thus declined as an independent political and military force, its headship ceased to be concentrated, the be of the Bizen area were drawn back into the levy system of the court, and the court used the occasion to bring the defence and the taxation of the Bizen, Bitchu and Harima line under more direct supervision. For the following decades the second half of the fifth century produced no rising of a local chief on the same scale in Yamato, while contacts with the Korean peninsula grew more frequent. What can be established is this: the war ended in a complete victory for the court, the chief was executed, the power was broken up and the order was rebuilt. What cannot be established is the course of the fighting, for the numbers of dead, the strengths, the dates, and even the composition of the participating units are almost entirely blank in the transmitted texts; the only certain items are the record of the execution of the chief and the sending of his head to the capital, and the outcome by which the court regained the Bizen front. That is why this remains a war whose result is known and whose process is not.
